newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Libya invites back stranded Palestinians.
newsitem.headline: Libya invites back stranded Palestinians.

text.p: Libya reversed course on Tuesday and said Palestinians stranded for more than a year on the Egypt-Libya border could return to Libya, the official Libyan news agency JANA said.

"The basic popular congresses invite the brother Palestinians on hunger strike at the Libyan-Egyptian border...to return inside the Arab Libyan lands," JANA, monitored in Tunis, quoted a source at the Libyan General People's Congress as saying.
The People's Congress is the decision-making body in Libya under national leader Muammar Gaddafi.
Hundreds of Palestinians have been stranded at the desert camp since September 1995 when Gaddafi ordered thousands of Palestinians to go home.
It was part of his campaign against the Palestinian peace accords with Israel, underlining that the agreement did not let the millions of Palestinians outside the occupied territories return home.
"For the time being, there is no possibility for the Palestinian people to return home in lands despoiled by the zionists (Israelis)," the Libyan Congress says.
Israel controls access to the autonomous West Bank and Gaza Strip and allows entry only to those with the status of residents.
Most Palestinians forced from Libya went to countries beyond Egypt but Egypt refused to admit those who had no proof they could continue to another country. They were stranded at the border.

Hundreds of those stranded, now in a second winter of freezing temperatures in flimsy tents on the road that connects Libya and Egypt, began a hunger strike last month to protest against their plight.
